pr_title: boards: beagle: beagleconnect_freedom: Use sky13317 antenna switch
pr_body:
- Use sky13317 device in dt instead of hack.
- Switch to using cc1352p1_launchxl board_antenna which also uses sky13317
- Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/71285
pr_comments: I'm not sure why the compliance check is failing here. Is it related to order of Kconfig parsing and thus a driver should be enabled in `Kconfig.*_defconfig`?

@Ayush1325 You will need to do a bit of cleanup while copying the driver, https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/83e8f1a2b0a75f719125f4c45f7a5d0c5f2f0594/drivers/misc/sky13317/sky13317.c#L52 _> drop this priority from board Kconfig.

@gmarull @nordicjm I have moved `rf_callback` and related stuff behind config variable since that will be specific to soc networking capabilities. The init code should be generic since everything for it is defined in dt. I have also made the bindings more specific by using dedicated v*-gpios for v1, v2 and v3 instead of bundling them together in gpios (similar to sky13351).

Does this seem better?

> not sure why I'm being asked to review again, when main concern hasn't been addressed

Can you please clarify what you wish to be changed here. I have moved the TI specific stuff behind CC1352P and CC1352P7 config variables. However, since the `rf_callback` will be dependent on the networking capabilities of the device, I am not sure what more can be done for it. 

I think I can split the soc dependent code to `sky13317_cc13xx*.c` or something but are you maybe looking for something else? It does not seem like `sky13351` has any driver either (although the dt binding is present), so I am not sure what I should look towards as sample for what a generic Zephyr antenna switch should look like.

Alternatively, it is also possible to keep this in the board-specific folder and have a copy for each board that uses it. However, this would make it difficult to keep the files in sync (similar to how current bcf does not share cc1352p1_launchxl `board_antenna.c` even though it can).

I have created another  PR which does not try to make a generic antenna switch bindings and just copies the current cc1352p1_launchxl antenna : #72332

I will close this PR in case that approach is preferable.

issue_context.title: Improve Beagleconnect Freedom board device tree
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
As pointed out in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64718 the `board_antenna.c`  beagleconnect freedom's handling of radio needs to be fixed to use device tree.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- [x] Move `BOARD_RF_HIGH_PA` and `BOARD_RF_SUB1GHZ` from `board_antenna.c` to device tree
- [x] Do not use `gpio-leds` for U.FL connector switch

review_comments: These SoC-specific attributes should be broken out separately than the switch driver.
should use the for each dts syntax
To make this more generic, these settings should come from the device-tree for the platform. These constants shouldn't go into a generic driver for the switch.
Are 'v1', 'v2', 'v3' somehow related to the hardware? If so, can we assign some meaning to connecting them via the device-tree?
They come from the [data sheet](https://www.skyworksinc.com/-/media/SkyWorks/Documents/Products/301-400/SKY13317-373LF_200914L.pdf). It is similar to how sky13351 names `vctl*-gpios`,

I think we still need a SoC specific antenna driver, but it should be able to use the device-tree settings to operate the antenna. The role of the SoC-specific driver is to connect the calls that switch the antenna (assigned through device-tree) to the SoC-specific calls on mode-changes that might require antenna switches. The Kconfig for custom HWattrs should enable the usage of the CC13x board antenna driver.

I have a problem with this driver, this is not a universal driver, no other platform can make use of this driver, the dts description lacks any sort of description for it and looking at the source file it essentially fits a device which has 2.4G output, PA output and sub-GHz output, so isn't at all generic and can't be used by any other board. @gmarull
@nordicjm while I agree with you, this is already used on another device in mainline. It would help if you could provide some more specific guidance. I'm trying to do the same.

Finding any generic antenna switching is looking difficult. https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/84e7107b32f9babdab7c74a7b2a3f96df1f5172b/samples/bluetooth/direction_finding_connectionless_tx/boards/nrf52833dk_nrf52833.overlay#L20 is not the least bit generic.

Avoid any SOC specific configs in this generic switch driver if at all possible. If this is just for pulling constants, pull them from device-tree entries and define those in the device-tree structure for this driver.
this is a no, as per the above comment
Hi. Can you take a look at #72332 ?
